Run CMSY++ for the Main Species of a Fishing Area

Source: R/cmsy_area.R
cmsy_area.Rd

This function does in one call what cmsy_input(), cmsy_run(), cmsy_plot(), cmsy_forecast() and cmsy_tables() do step by step, for the species with the largest catch in an FAO fishing area (or for chosen species): it prepares the catch-only input, runs CMSY++ on every stock, draws the charts, projects the stocks under fishing scenarios and writes the tables. Progress bars follow each step.

Usage

cmsy_area(
  area,
  top = 10,
  species = NULL,
  recent_years = 10,
  out_dir = "cmsy_areas",
  auto_start = TRUE,
  seed = 1,
  parallel = NULL,
  settings = list(),
  charts = c(cmsy_stock_charts, cmsy_summary_charts),
  classes = c("fao", "palomares"),
  forecast = TRUE,
  annotations = getOption("faofishingreport.cmsy_annotations", FALSE),
  lang = NULL,
  pptx = getOption("faofishingreport.pptx", FALSE),
  silent = fao_setting("silent"),
  ...
)

Arguments

area

FAO major fishing area name(s), as in fishing_area_data() (e.g. "Atlantic, Eastern Central"), or FAO catch data such as fishing_area_data()$area_data.

top

Number of species with the largest catch to assess. Default is 10.

species

Optional species to assess instead of the top ones, by English or Chinese name, scientific name or FAO 3-alpha code.

recent_years

Catch is ranked by its mean over the last recent_years years of the data. Default is 10.

out_dir

The folder in which a folder per area is made. Default is "cmsy_areas".

auto_start

As in cmsy_run(), but TRUE by default here: a stock whose start biomass is ambiguous starts in the first year with at least 40% of the maximum catch, as suggested by CMSY++.

seed

The random seed of the runs, so that the results can be repeated. Default is 1.

parallel

The number of stocks run at the same time. Each uses two more processes for its two MCMC chains. Default is half the number of processor cores.

settings

Optional named list of CMSY++ settings that replace its defaults, e.g. list(CV.C = 0.2, n.iter = 100000, n.burnin = 50000). See cmsy_defaults() for the settings, their defaults and what they do. Default is no change: CMSY++ runs with its own defaults. The settings used are saved in settings_used.csv of the run folder and in result$settings.

charts

The charts to draw (see cmsy_plot()). Default is all of them.

classes

The status classes: "fao" (default, two classes) or "palomares" (five classes).

forecast

A logical value. If TRUE (default), the stocks are also projected under the default fishing scenarios of cmsy_forecast().

annotations

The text added to the axis titles and labels: FALSE (default) none, TRUE all, or any of "title", "subtitle", "caption", "legend" and "labels" (text inside the chart). The default can be changed for the session with options(faofishingreport.cmsy_annotations = TRUE).

lang

The language of the chart text and names: "en" (English), "zh" (Chinese) or "both" (Chinese and English). Default is NULL, which uses the language set with fao_settings() ("en" unless changed).

pptx

A logical value. If TRUE, the charts are also saved as editable PowerPoint files in <out_dir>/<area>/figures_pptx/. Default is FALSE, which can be changed for all functions with fao_settings(pptx = TRUE).

silent

A logical value. If FALSE (default), a progress bar shows how many stocks have finished, with the elapsed and the estimated remaining time, and messages report the run. If TRUE, nothing is printed. The default can be changed for the session with fao_settings(silent = TRUE).

...

Further arguments passed to cmsy_input() (e.g. priors, default_resilience).

Value

Invisibly, the result of cmsy_run() with the elements input, forecast, tables and dir (the folder of the area); a list of these, named by area, for several areas.

Details

The results of each area are saved in their own folder, out_dir/<area>/:

input/

the CMSY++ catch and ID files, the stocks used, and the main species left out with the reason (e.g. no r prior: see priors and default_resilience of cmsy_input());

runs/

the CMSY++ run of each stock (its folder has the original CMSY++ charts, output and log), the changed CMSY++ code and the list of changes;

figures/

one folder of charts per stock and a summary/ folder for all stocks (PNG, and PowerPoint in figures_pptx/ when pptx is TRUE);

tables/

results, yearly series, the priors and results tables for reports, projections, the CMSY++ settings used (settings_used.csv) and the sources of everything used (sources.csv).

As in cmsy_input(), FAO data have catches only (no abundance index), so all stocks are assessed with the catch-only part of CMSY++ and the results are indicative.

References

Froese, R., Winker, H., Coro, G., Palomares, M.L.D., Tsikliras, A.C., Dimarchopoulou, D., Touloumis, K., Demirel, N., Vianna, G.M.S., Scarcella, G., Schijns, R., Liang, C. and Pauly, D. (2023). New developments in the analysis of catch time series as the basis for fish stock assessments: the CMSY++ method. Acta Ichthyologica et Piscatoria 53: 173-189. doi:10.3897/aiep.53.105910

Froese, R., Demirel, N., Coro, G. and Winker, H. (2021). User Guide for CMSY++. GEOMAR, Germany, 17 pp. https://oceanrep.geomar.de/id/eprint/52147/

FAO (2026). The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2026. Rome, FAO. Section "The status of fishery resources", Box 1.3 (assessment tiers and status classes). https://openknowledge.fao.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/09d03e2f-7097-4d59-bf94-db65e95f44fd/content/sofia-2026/the-status-fishery-resources.html

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cmsy_setup()                     # once: JAGS and the R packages CMSY++ needs

# The ten species with the largest catch of the last ten years in FAO area 34, in Chinese
area34 <- cmsy_area("Atlantic, Eastern Central", top = 10, lang = "zh")
area34$summary[, c("Stock", "species_name", "B_Bmsy", "F_Fmsy", "status")]
area34$dir                       # folder with input/, runs/, figures/ and tables/

# Chosen species (scientific name, FAO code, ...), all annotations, five status classes
cmsy_area("Atlantic, Eastern Central", species = c("Brachydeuterus auritus", "PIL"),
          annotations = TRUE, classes = "palomares")

# Species without a FishBase prior get a resilience (passed on to cmsy_input())
cmsy_area("Atlantic, Eastern Central", top = 20, default_resilience = "Medium")

# Several areas, quietly, with longer MCMC chains (see cmsy_defaults())
cmsy_area(c("Atlantic, Eastern Central", "Pacific, Northwest"), top = 5, silent = TRUE,
          settings = list(n.iter = 100000, n.burnin = 50000))
} # }
